cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle costs 60 Rupees. This is stated in the Quest 2 overworld walkthrough ("Buy a Blue Candle (for 60 R)") and in the Quest 1 overworld guide ("You can purchase the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees").

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need at least five Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items entry. The Overworld Quest 1 guide mentions six heart containers, and the Hyrule 3 guide also states five.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level-3 of the first quest, you can obtain the Raft, a Heart Container, the third Piece of Triforce, and the Map (found by heading right from the four door room).

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4 and is four times as powerful as the wooden sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. A fairy fills 3 of Link's hearts when defeated as an enemy drop, and in the fairy ponds a fairy fills all of your heart meters.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: Hyrulian men are fond of gambling and will play the Money Making game with anyone willing to part with their rupees. The documents do not describe the Money Making game's rules or how to win in it.

cases.question: What does the old man in Level-4 of the first quest say?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" at the start of the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents do not say whether the name is case-sensitive, so it is not confirmed that "ZELDA" in all capitals triggers the same result.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
cases.answer: You can buy the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees by walking through the door one screen west of the green rocks area (reached from the Fairy Fountain route described in Quest 1). It can light up dark rooms in dungeons, burn bushes in the overworld, and damage enemies, but it can only be used once per screen.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
cases.answer: The boss of Level 1 in the first quest is Aquamentus. Strike him in the head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between the energy orbs he emits from his horn. Only the Magical Shield absorbs the orbs; blocking with the regular shield causes damage, and with sword beams you can hit any part of his body.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Level-4 in the first quest, and which item is inside?
cases.answer: To enter Level 4 in the first quest, you need the Raft. Inside, the objectives list obtaining the Ladder, a Heart Container (after defeating the 2-headed Gleeok), and the fourth Piece of Triforce.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The dragon boss is Aquamentus, with 6 HP. It shoots fireballs that split in three directions and can only be blocked by the Magical Shield. It is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows, and can also be killed by two Bombs.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: To defeat Gleeok, stab each attached head until it breaks free and flies around the room, then destroy every one of the attached heads; a free head is still a threat and cannot be defeated on its own. Defeating the boss earns a Heart Container.

cases.question: How do I use the Hookshot?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: Can I ride a horse in this game?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: In the first quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: The documents do not state which first-quest dungeon contains the Ladder. Dungeon 4 of Quest 1 lists obtaining the Ladder as an objective, but that only shows the Ladder is a goal there, not that it is found there.

cases.question: In the second quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: The documents do not directly say which second-quest dungeon contains the Ladder as a dungeon item. Dungeon 6 of Quest 2 lists "Obtain the Ladder" as an objective, and Dungeon 7 lists the Ladder as a pre-requisite, so the Ladder is obtained in Quest 2 Dungeon 6.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: The documents mention a few ways to attack in Zelda 1: Link's sword (e.g., Darknut is vulnerable from the back and sides to the sword, sword beam, or magical rod), Bombs (which harm Darknut and are the only way to harm Dodongo), and attacking enemies from a ladder, which lets Link attack without reprisal. However, the documents do not give a general guide to all attack methods.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. You can also press the B button to use your selected subweapon, such as the Magical Wand.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button on the NES controller to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map, change subweapon, etc. Pressing Start again returns you from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes, bombs can blast holes in weak walls. The Items document states that the bomb can be used to kill enemies or blast holes in weak walls.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Items above the blue box on the sub-screen are used automatically. Only one item in the blue box can be assigned to the B button, and you change that assignment by switching to the sub-screen.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. You can also use your B button to fire a subweapon, such as the Magical Wand, which fires even if you don't have full life.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: The documents mention several healing sources: a flashing Heart refills one full heart, a Fairy fills 3 hearts (in Fairy ponds, a Fairy fills all hearts), and a Water of Life completely refills your life bar. You can also return to the Fairy Fountain to heal, as stated in the Blue Candle walkthrough.

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: Money can be found in several places. In the 1st Quest, bombing the wall right of the crack at B-4 on Hyrule 8 reveals a cave with a Red Moblin who gives 30 Rupees. In the 2nd Quest, burning the lower left tree at D-2 on Hyrule 8 leads to a Red Moblin who gives 100 Rupees, and burning the lower right tree at B-2 reveals a stairwell with 10 Rupees. You can also bomb a rock face immediately left of the start screen to reach the Money Making Game cave for earning rupees.

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: One documented method is a cheat: when you enter the first dungeon, immediately leave and come back, and the locked door will open. Otherwise, each Key opens one door, and you can carry up to nine keys until you obtain the Magic Key.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is likely Aquamentus, which has 6 HP and shoots fireballs that split in three directions; it can only be blocked by the Magical Shield. It is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows, and can also be killed by two Bombs. Gleeok is also a dragon, with two, three or four heads that must each be attacked.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: The documents say to fight and defeat the Moblins in the nearby area until they drop Bombs that you can collect. Quest 2 also lists getting some Bombs as an early step, but without a specific location.

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: The documents don't say how to unlock the Bow directly. They do say the Bow is obtained in Quest 1 Dungeon 1 and Quest 2 Dungeon 5 as an objective, and that you must purchase Arrows from a shop before you can use it.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: Choose "SAVE" with Select and press Start on the Game Over screen; the game then stores your accomplishments until you next play. You can also press Up (D-pad) and A simultaneously on controller 2 from the sub-screen menu for quick access to the Save Screen.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: Documents mention a few ways: a Fairy drop fills 3 of Link's hearts, and fairy ponds fill all heart meters. You can also get the sixth Heart Container by setting a bomb on the lower-right corner of a huge rock in the middle of the screen one screen west of the eastern mountains' seashore path. Extra Heart Containers are also listed as treasures in several levels, such as the Raft, Stepladder, and Magical Sword levels.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes, a Magical Shield can be bought in Quest 1 for 90 Rupees from a shop revealed by burning a tree in the green forest, after getting to the seashore area. In Quest 2, a Magic Shield can be bought for 90 R using the Blue Candle on Lake Hylia.

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: Dark rooms in dungeons can be lit with a candle; the Dungeon 4 walkthrough says you can light them with the Blue Candle. The Blue Candle can only be used once per screen, while the Red Candle has the same effect with no limit per screen.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air. Jump height is fixed regardless of how long you hold it.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points to throw.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump towards and cling to a wall, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back towards it. Done correctly, you rise and cling to the wall higher than where you started, and repeating this can climb to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead as soon as you enter the hall.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The documents do not identify a boss of Stage 3-3 specifically. Chunk 006 says the boss of Act III is Basaquer, and Act III includes Stage 3-3, so Basaquer is the boss of Act III, though the documents do not explicitly tie that boss to Stage 3-3 itself.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
cases.answer: The Fire Wheel surrounds Ryu with a circle of fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts him. It requires no spirit points to use, but it replaces any secondary weapon you hold and disappears after five seconds.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the B button to attack by swinging your sword. You can attack low by squatting when you attack. To use a secondary weapon, hold Up on the D-pad while pressing B, provided you have enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: how do i heal?
cases.answer: Collect health potions, which restore six lost bars of health from your meter. Potions appear in stages, such as a lamp on the left after the bridge in Stage 4-2 and a candle above the first potion in Stage 5-2.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: The documents say that if you lose to any of the final bosses in Stage 6-3 (after going through its door), you are returned all the way to 6-1, regardless of remaining lives. Also, losing a boss fight can send you back to an earlier moment in the Act, and dying after defeating the Masked Devil sends you back to 6-1 to face Jaquio with spirit power.

cases.question: What is the password to skip to Act 5?
cases.answer: The documents do not contain a password to skip to Act 5. They state that you may not select or skip any level and must play every stage in order.

cases.question: How do I unlock the second playable character?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.
